title: After UNEP MARS alerts, operators divert gas from an Iraqi flare that had released about 1.7m tCO2e since 2023; the source may be in the Zubair field near Basra
summary: The Chemical Engineer (5 May 2026), relaying UNEP: the largest source mitigated in 2026 was an Iraqi flare, 1.7m tCO2e since 2023, apparently in the Zubair field; Eni did not confirm closure.
account: The Chemical Engineer reported on 5 May 2026, relaying UNEP's Methane Alert and Response System (MARS) figures. MARS had curbed 41 methane super-emitters since launching in 2023. Six significant sources had stopped emitting in 2026 following MARS alerts, including three in Turkmenistan and one each in Libya, Iraq and Kazakhstan. The largest source mitigated this year was a flare in Iraq, where operators diverted gas to a newer facility. The flare had released an estimated 1.7m tCO2e since 2023. The source appears to have been at a facility in the Zubair oil and gas field near Basra. The article reports that the operator Eni acknowledged running a leak detection and repair campaign at Zubair. Eni did not confirm closure of the specific source. The article says MARS uses data from 35 satellite instruments to identify large plumes and alert operators. UNEP's MARS page adds that IMEO couples satellite data with scientific expertise and advanced AI models. No date for the mitigation is given beyond 2026. UNEP's press releases were not available, and no UNEP case document for this source is on record.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators mitigate them. This case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); facility operators in Iraq (gas diversion); the article names Eni as operator of the Zubair field
location: Zubair oil and gas field near Basra, Iraq (location reported as apparent, not confirmed)
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas production; intergovernmental observatory

ratings.reason: Operators are reported to have diverted gas to a newer facility. The operator did not confirm the specific closure, and no operational detail or cost is documented.
Reported as the largest source mitigated in 2026, after an estimated 1.7m tCO2e released since 2023. It is still one case among about 41 confirmed, and unconfirmed by the operator.

ai_role.statement: The trade press credits the mitigation to MARS alerts. Only UNEP's general page describes MARS as satellite-based with advanced AI models, so the AI contribution to this detection is not isolated. A single news item relaying the system operator documents the case. The named field operator declined to confirm closure of the specific source.
